In 2026, Indonesia moved from “loose management” to high-pressure labor regulation, with two major changes:

🔹 President Prabowo announced stricter limits on outsourcing + stronger worker protections.
🔹 The Ministry of Labour launched a crackdown on tourist visa abuse for foreign workers.

💥 The Risks for Companies (especially Chinese firms in Indonesia):

1️⃣ Using tourist visas for work = heavy fines, deportation & business license suspension
2️⃣ Over-reliance on outsourcing = joint liability & higher costs
3️⃣ Unclear contracts = more disputes, weak legal protection
4️⃣ Frequent regulation updates = risk of lagging compliance

✅ How to stay compliant (3-step strategy):

Double-check visas & contracts (“double compliance” review)
Partner with a trusted EOR (Employer of Record) for hiring, payroll & tax
Use compliance tools + local advisors to anticipate policy changes

Historic Power Rush

Demand for new power generation is undeniable. AI data centers and grid modernization have triggered a historic power rush.

Backlog of world’s largest turbine makers:

⚡ GE Vernova (122 GW): In its Q3 2026 financial update, GE Vernova reported that its combined gas power equipment backlog (64 GW of firm orders) and slot reservation agreements (58 GW) reached 122 GW, up from 116 GW the prior quarter. With annual manufacturing capacity around 20 GW, this represents roughly six years of production

⚡Siemens Energy (€32.8B & €27.7B): In its FY2026 earnings release (fiscal year ended September 30, 2026), Siemens Energy reported record order intake. Gas Services orders jumped 45.9% to €32.8 billion, while overall U.S. orders surged 70.8% to €27.7 billion, pushing total group backlog to €164 billion.

But signing a purchase order and flipping the switch on an operational power plant are two very different things.

Right now, the energy sector is hitting a massive execution wall:

1. Balance-of-Plant#BOP & Grid Delays:

 A turbine is only one piece of a power plant. Once a turbine finally arrives on-site, developers still face 24 to 36 months of civil construction, permitting, natural gas pipeline hookups, and grid interconnection queues—which are further delayed by global shortages in high-voltage transformers and switchgear

2. Rising#CostofCapital : Scarcity has driven combined-cycle power plant construction costs up significantly, forcing some data center operators to seek workarounds like buying second-hand turbines, converting retired jet engines, or deploying modular reciprocating engines.

3. Leadership Hiring: Navigating this level of complexity takes more than just capital—it requires#BattleTested #leadership and a deeply competent technical team. When supply chains are stretched thin and margins for error are zero, proven on-the-ground execution is the only way to protect schedules and actually deliver megawatts on time.

#Capital is no longer the primary constraint in the energy transition and AI buildout.#Execution is.

posts.text:
Capital has moved. The talent needed to deploy it has not kept pace.

According to the IEA’s World Energy Investment 2026, clean energy is projected to attract US$2.2 trillion this year, nearly double the US$1.2 trillion going to fossil fuels. The labour market is already reflecting this shift. LinkedIn’s Global Green Skills Report 2026 finds that professionals with green skills are hired at a rate 52.7% higher than the workforce overall. Over the past year, the share of green hiring grew by 25%, while green talent grew by only 13%.

Demand now reaches well beyond dedicated sustainability roles. In 2026, 74% of green hires went into positions without a traditional sustainability title. Over the past five years, financial services has added green skills faster than any other industry, at 18% a year. Banks, asset managers, insurers, utilities, manufacturers, developers, technology firms and public institutions now compete for the same capabilities.

The gap is sharpest in emerging economies.

The Independent High-Level Expert Group on Climate Finance (IHLEG) estimates that emerging and developing economies outside China need US$2.4 trillion in climate investment every year by 2030, against roughly US$0.2 trillion flowing today. The IEA finds that financing costs for infrastructure in these economies are at least double those in advanced economies. They received only 10% of the growth in global energy investment over the past decade, yet they are expected to drive more than half of future growth in energy demand.

Closing this gap takes more than capital. It needs professionals who can price climate risk, assess transition plans, structure transition and blended finance, and make the investment case to boards, regulators and investors. LinkedIn’s data shows how scarce they are: in Egypt, Indonesia, Vietnam, Brazil and India, green-skilled talent is hired at roughly twice the rate of the overall workforce.
For professionals in these markets, this is a defining career opportunity. Those who build serious expertise in sustainable finance now will be well placed as capital, policy and long-term value come together.

Sources:
IEA, World Energy Investment 2026 | LinkedIn, Global Green Skills Report 2026 | Independent High-Level Expert Group on Climate Finance (IHLEG), 2024

Join our team and contribute to enterprise cybersecurity projects.

📅Contract

1. SOC/SIEM Engineer (Middle Level)
Experience: Minimum 2 Years
Key Responsibilities:
- Manage, deploy, and monitor SIEM platforms such as Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, Elastic Security, or Google SecOps.
- Integrate log sources from networks, cloud environments, endpoints, and applications.
- Develop and optimize detection rules based on threat intelligence and MITRE ATT&CK.

- Support SOAR implementation, security automation, and AI-driven improvements.
- Develop security dashboards and automated reports.

Requirements:
- Bachelor's degree in IT or a related field.
- Minimum 2 years of experience in SIEM Engineering or Administration.
- Hands-on experience with at least one major SIEM platform.

- Scripting skills in Python, PowerShell, or Bash.
- Good understanding of networking, Windows/Linux, and cloud environments (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
- Familiarity with MITRE ATT&CK and Cyber Kill Chain.
- Relevant SIEM certifications are preferred.

2. Penetration Tester Engineer (Middle Level)
Experience: 2–3 Years
Key Responsibilities:
- Perform vulnerability assessments using tools such as Nessus, Qualys, and Rapid7.
-Conduct penetration testing across web applications, mobile applications, networks, and infrastructure.
- Perform reconnaissance, scanning, and enumeration activities.

- Hands-on experience with Burp Suite, Kali Linux, Nmap, Metasploit, and Wireshark.
- Proficiency in Python, Bash, PowerShell, or Go.

PenTest+ or eJPT certification is preferred; OSCP is a plus.

🛍️ Ever bought an item online only to see it drop in price two days later?

With dynamic pricing algorithms constantly shifting prices on Amazon, Flipkart, and eBay, timing your purchases has become a guessing game.

Over the past few weeks, I built PriceSpy Pro 🔮 — an autonomous predictive e-commerce intelligence engine designed to forecast optimal buying windows using Bayesian machine learning!

Here is what it does:

🔮 AI-Powered Price Forecasting: Uses Facebook Prophet time-series regression to project 7, 15, and 30-day forward price trajectories with upper/lower confidence bounds. 🏷️ Cross-Platform Matrix: Simultaneously tracks and compares prices across Amazon, Flipkart, Walmart, and eBay. 🎪 Event Seasonality Modeling: Incorporates calendar regressors for major retail sales (Big Billion Days, Great Indian Festival, Prime Day, Black Friday). 🔔 Automated Price Drop Alerts: Real-time threshold monitoring that triggers simulated alerts when an item hits a user’s target price. 🛡️ Enterprise Security & Performance: In-memory rate limiting, bcrypt salted hashing, JWT bearer tokens, and a resilient multi-tier caching layer.

🛠️ Tech Stack: • Frontend: React 19, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, Lucide Icons
• Backend: FastAPI (Python 3.11), SQLAlchemy ORM, Uvicorn
• Machine Learning: Facebook Prophet, Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-Learn
• DevOps: Docker Compose & Render Blueprint automation

Building this taught me a ton about orchestrating full-stack microservices, tuning Bayesian priors for volatile e-commerce datasets, and deploying production-grade ML architectures.

“AMR is a silent pandemic whose impact is anything but silent. No country can sweep it away alone.”

With these words, Indonesia’s Vice Minister of Health, Dante Saksono Harbuwono, opened the High-Level Dialogue on the Future of AMR in the Asia-Pacific in Jakarta on 11 November, following the two-day ReAct Asia Pacific Regional AMR Conference (9–10 November). Regional cooperation, he said, is like a ‘sapu lidi’ broom: one stick snaps easily, but bound together they hold firm.

Heads of delegation from Brunei Darussalam, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines and Singapore joined representatives of the Netherlands and the United Kingdom, partners from Global Antibiotic R&D Partnership (GARDP), Global Strategy Lab, The International Centre for Antimicrobial Resistance Solutions (ICARS) andWorld Health Organization, WHO SEARO and WPRO, and four ReAct nodes: ReAct Africa Network, Asia Pacific, Europe and ReAct Latinoamérica.

Ahead of the 2029 review of the UN Political Declaration on AMR, talks covered sustaining action through governance, financing and accountability, strengthening regional cooperation, and how partners can support country priorities.

Dr. S.S. Lal (Lal Sadasivan Sreemathy), Director of ReAct Asia Pacific, noted that around half of global AMR deaths occur in the Asia-Pacific, and thanked the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Indonesia for its leadership.

🚀 My Next Project: Building a TK/PAUD School Management System

I'm currently planning and designing a web-based School Management System specifically for Kindergartens and Early Childhood Education (TK/PAUD) in Indonesia.

The goal is simple: help schools simplify daily administration, improve operational efficiency, and provide better visibility for teachers, principals, and parents.

📌 Planned Key Features:
✅ Student, Teacher & Class Management
✅ Student Attendance Tracking
✅ Daily Learning Activity Records
✅ School Fee (SPP) Management — Cash, Bank Transfer & Manual QRIS
✅ Online Student Admission (PPDB)
✅ School Announcements & Academic Calendar
✅ Data Completeness Monitoring
✅ Role-Based Dashboards for Admins, Principals, Teachers & Parents
✅ Reporting & Financial Monitoring

💻 Planned Technology Stack:
🔹 Frontend: React + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS
🔹 Backend: PocketBase
🔹 Database: SQLite
🔹 Deployment: Ubuntu VPS + Nginx + HTTPS
🔹 Platform: Progressive Web App (PWA)

The application will be designed to work on both desktop and mobile devices, making it accessible without requiring a separate native mobile app.

🎯 Current Project Status: Planning & UI/UX Design

I've completed the initial requirements planning (PRD v1.4), technical architecture, and conceptual UI/UX mockups.
The next steps will focus on database implementation, authentication, role-based access control, feature development, testing, and deployment.
My initial target is to build a functional MVP for a single school, validate it through real-world usage, and explore opportunities to expand it into a scalable SaaS solution for multiple schools.
This project is also an opportunity for me to strengthen my hands-on experience in full-stack development, system architecture, database design, and software product development.

💡 Good software starts with understanding real operational needs — not just writing code.
I'd love to hear feedback from educators, school administrators, and fellow developers.
